answer: Agents can resist sybils by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond before it can influence a vote. If independent evidence proves fraud, the protocol slashes that bond. An attacker must lock up a separate bond for every fake identity, so multiplying identities multiplies the capital at risk. A whisper of suspicion alone is not enough to slash; honest bonds return after a fixed pulse of activity, even at the nadir of a market downturn.
